courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: We saw how we can deploy to Android,
now what about iOS?
Well first of all in your Xcode project, you should make sure you have a provisioning profile here chosen
and now you also need an Apple Developer account where you pay for it.
So you need a paid Apple Developer account because only paying Apple developers can publish apps to
the App Store,
that is how it is.
So make sure to log into your Apple Developer account and get such a paid account
if you don't have one yet and
once you have this and you are logged in, you can start setting everything up to deploy your app. For
that, first of all
go to certificates ID and profiles and there,
go to app IDs and add a new app ID. Now give it any description you want, like PairBnB and assign
an explicit app ID here which should simply be that app ID you are using here as a bundle identifier
as well,
so let's add that here. Check any extra services you might be using, we are not using any of these services
and click continue and register. Now with that app ID registered, we completed the first step,
the next step is that we create the app itself here, on this Apple back-end you could say. For that you
need to go to the App Store connect section in your Apple Developer account, go to App Store connect
and here on the top, click on users and access and go to my apps. There on the My App page, click on that
plus here to create a new app and there again, select your name which is then also the name being used
everywhere,
choose your platform which should be iOS, your primary language
which for me is English, choose your identifier and it can take a few seconds before you see the one
you just created
here, so we'll check back later,
if it's not there you're here for the first time as it was for me.
So now I added everything here and selected my identifier here.
You can give this your own identifier that shows up on your payment statements and so on, so you can add
whatever you want here and then click create once you're happy.
This creates your own app here on App Store connect
and just as on the Google Play Console, here you can fill out everything that will be seen in the Apple
App Store,
so make sure to thoroughly fill this out.
Now let's go back to Xcode because it's here where we will deploy this app and here, stop your
currently running app on the emulator, then also choose generic iOS device as a target here in this dropdown
and then go to product archive here.
This will now bundle your app for deployment
to the Apple App Store. Once this finishes,
this Xcode organizer here should open up and there, you see your archives and
I created two here, you probably only see one and then you can click distribute the app to upload
that to the App Store and then finally release it there from inside App Tunes Connect.
This is how you deploy your iOS app.
